Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views

Class TableSpec

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views.TableSpec
public final class TableSpec extends Object
Java description of one datatables view: data source, columns, ribbon, row styling, row actions, row detail, selection and bulk actions. It replaces hand-written <@card type="datatables"> JSON5 for apps that build pages in Java, and toCardBody() serializes to exactly the card body the FTL path produces. All behavior (paging, search, rendering, actions) stays in juneau-views.js; this type never calls a card-type handler directly — see the class's rendering note on toCardBody().

Column.defaultVisible(false) only hides a column when the client's columnConfig (juneau-config.js) is on.

Example:

TableSpec t = TableSpec.create("slo") .rowType(SloPod.class) .dataUrl("/rest/slo/data") .defaultOrder("pod", TableSpec.Sort.ASC) .columns( Column.create("pod").label("Pod").className("ssc-id-cell"), Column.create("incidentKey").label("Incident").render("linked").href("{incidentUrl}"), Column.create("rootCause").label("Root cause").defaultVisible(false)) .ribbon(RibbonItem.refresh(), RibbonItem.export("copy", "csv")) .rowClass("analysisState", Op.EQ, "degraded", "row-degraded") .rowActions(RowAction.create("analyze").label("Analyze pod") .endpoint("/rest/slo/analyze").method(RowAction.Method.POST)) .detail(RowDetail.create("/rest/slo/data/{id}").title("{pod}") .region(RegionDef.create("slo-detail").populate("slo-detail"))); t.validate(); Map<String,Object> body = t.toCardBody(); // the unwrapped catalog

Since:
10.0.0

    • urlState

      public TableSpec urlState(String... names)
      Declares URL-state directives this table's address bar carries, so their values reach the table's server requests.

      Each name selects one of the built-in directives (day, ids or window); any other name is refused, because this method does not register codecs and the page contract only carries the built-ins. A name not yet declared is emitted as an empty configuration object, which means the directive's defaults; a name already declared keeps its configuration (for example a day param set by urlStateDayParam(String)). This method never clears configuration. Directives are emitted in the order they were first declared. The call is atomic: every name is validated before any is declared, so if one is refused nothing is changed.

      Parameters:
      names - The directive names; each one of day, ids or window.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If a name is null, blank or not a built-in directive.

    • urlStateDayParam

      public TableSpec urlStateDayParam(String param)
      Declares the day URL-state directive and names the request query parameter it sends the selected day under.

      urlState("day") sends the day as a day parameter; this form is for a server whose parameter has another name. The directive is emitted as urlState.day.param, in the position day was first declared. Calling this again replaces the parameter name (the last call wins).

      Parameters:
      param - The query-parameter name; must match ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If param is null, blank, or malformed.

    • urlState

      public TableSpec urlState(String name, Map<String,Object> config)
      Declares a URL-state directive together with its options.

      This is the configurable form of urlState(String...) for the three built-in directives; every option the client's built-in codecs accept can be expressed, so a page needs no hand-written map to configure one:

      • ids — param (request parameter name, default ids) and max (an integer >= 1, default 200).
      • window — params, a map that may hold start and/or end (the request parameter names, defaults start/end).
      • day — param (request parameter name, default day); same as urlStateDayParam(String).
      Any other directive name is refused: this method does not register codecs, and the page contract only carries the built-ins.

      Restrictions (deliberate, so the wire contract and the builder agree): every parameter name must match ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ (the same grammar as day.param), and max must be an integer (Integer, Long, Short or Byte) of at least 1. The client's own fallbacks for a falsy, string or fractional max, or for an unusual parameter name, are refused here rather than reproduced. The result is the same value an FTL page writes as urlState: {ids:{param:'pid',max:50}}.

      Merge, not replace. The options are merged into any entry already declared for name: each option given here overwrites the same option declared earlier (the last call wins, as with urlStateDayParam(String)), options not named here are kept, and window.params is merged key by key. Like urlState(String...) this never clears configuration, and an empty map just declares the directive. The directive keeps the position it was first declared in. The call is atomic: if any option is refused, nothing is changed.

      Parameters:
      name - The directive name; one of day, ids or window.
      config - The directive options; deep-copied, so later changes to the map have no effect. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the name is null, blank or not a built-in directive, the config is null, or an option is unknown for a built-in directive, mistyped, or out of range (a parameter name that is malformed, a max that is not a positive integer, a window.params key other than start/end).

    • toCardBody

      public JsonMap toCardBody()
      Builds this table's catalog-form card body, with no contractVersion anywhere (the client stamps every contract version). This is the only place in this type that knows the datatables wire shape. The result is the unwrapped catalog the datatables card type reads, and is rendered the same single way <@card> is, by the page mixin's cardTypes.toCard(CardSource.create("datatables", id()) .bodyMap(toCardBody()).build()); this type never calls a card-type handler directly.

      The body holds only plain data (maps, lists, strings, numbers, booleans), the same shape a parsed body has.

      Each column carries its effective operator set (its own, else operators(SearchOperatorSet)).

      Returns:
      The catalog, with keys in a fixed order and absent optional values omitted.
